lumio
Lumio
Chapter 11 — Mar 2024

Lumio, a residential solar installer that operated in several states including California, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2024. It also did business under the name 1st Light Energy, so permits and paperwork on older systems may carry either name.

Lumio's installation and workmanship warranties depend on a company that no longer services customers. Equipment sold with the system, such as panels, inverters and batteries, carries its own manufacturer warranty.

Your Lumio workmanship warranty is effectively gone. Manufacturer equipment warranties usually still apply, but someone has to diagnose the fault and file the claim. We do both for Lumio and 1st Light Energy systems.
simply-solar
Simply Solar
Chapter 11 — Jul 2026

Simply Solar, headquartered in Rancho Cucamonga, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 2026. It served homeowners across Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino and San Diego counties, among others.

Because the filing is recent, some customers still have systems under construction, awaiting inspection or waiting on utility approval. Others have working systems and no one to call if something fails.

If your Simply Solar system is installed but not approved to operate, or it has stopped producing, we can inspect it independently, tell you where it stands and what is needed to finish or fix it. Your contract and any loan terms are between you and those parties; we do not change them.
solare-energy
Solare Energy
Closed — 2026
Solare Energy was a San Diego County solar installer operating since 1989, one of the largest in the region. The company closed in 2026.

With decades of installs across San Diego County, many Solare systems are now old enough that inverters and monitoring hardware are reaching the end of their expected life, and the installer that knew the system is gone.

Older Solare systems often need an inverter replacement, a monitoring update or a performance check. We service San Diego County homes directly and can tell you what is still covered by the equipment manufacturers.
posigen
PosiGen
Chapter 11 — Nov 2025

PosiGen filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2025. It focused on solar for low-to-moderate-income homeowners and served customers in about 13 states, including California, often through leases and power purchase agreements rather than outright purchase.
If you lease or buy your system through PosiGen, your payment and ownership terms sit with PosiGen or whoever takes over its contracts. Service and repairs are a separate question from the financing.
We do not change your lease or loan. We can inspect the equipment independently, tell you whether it is producing what it should, and explain which repairs the manufacturer warranties cover.
sunworks
Sunworks / Solcius
Chapter 7 — Feb 2024

Sunworks filed for Chapter 7 liquidation in February 2024. Its subsidiary Solcius, a Santa Ana installer that Sunworks had acquired in 2021, collapsed along with it. Permits and contracts may carry either name.
Chapter 7 means the company stopped operating. Unlike a restructuring, there is no successor to honor service calls or workmanship warranties.

Workmanship coverage from Sunworks or Solcius is gone. Equipment warranties from the manufacturers generally survive. We can diagnose the system, file manufacturer claims and do the labor the installer used to do.
infinity-energy
Infinity Energy
Ceased operations — 2023
Infinity Energy, based in Rocklin, California, was one of the largest residential solar installers in the state, with a focus on power purchase agreements. It ceased operations in 2023.
Many Infinity customers are on PPAs, which means the equipment may be owned by a third party. Check your agreement to see who owns and maintains the system before you authorize repairs.

If the equipment is yours, we can service it. If a PPA owner holds the system, we can still inspect it and document the fault so the owner can act. Either way you get a straight answer about what is wrong.
suntuity
Suntuity Renewables
Shut down — about 2024
Suntuity Renewables sold and installed solar in several states, including California, New Jersey and Texas. The company shut down around 2024.
With the company gone, nothing remains of its service desk or workmanship warranty. Equipment warranties from the panel and inverter makers are the part that still has value.
We can read your system, check production against your utility bill, and tell you what is covered and what is not.
adt-solar
ADT Solar / SunPro Solar
Shut down — Jan 2023

ADT Solar shut down in January 2023, ending its solar business across about 22 states. The company had acquired SunPro Solar in 2021 and rebranded it, so older permits and paperwork may say SunPro Solar.
The security brand ADT still exists, but the solar business does not provide service. Calling ADT will not reach anyone who can repair your system.
If your system was installed by ADT Solar or SunPro Solar, the workmanship warranty is gone. We can inspect it, find the fault and file claims with the equipment manufacturers.
pink-energy
Pink Energy
Chapter 7 — Oct 2022
Pink Energy, formerly Power Home Solar, filed for Chapter 7 liquidation in October 2022. It sold in about 17 states.
Chapter 7 closed the company for good. Some customers also have financing that continues with a lender even though the installer is gone.
Your loan, if you have one, is separate from repairs. We can inspect the system independently and tell you whether the equipment is working and what the manufacturers will cover.
harness-power
Harness Power
Shut down — spring 2023
Harness Power, a Pasadena-based installer, shut down abruptly in spring 2023, citing insurmountable financial challenges. It served the Los Angeles area.
Customers were left with systems and no installer to contact for repairs, monitoring problems or warranty claims.
We service Los Angeles County systems directly. A free evaluation shows how your system is performing and which equipment warranties still apply.
vision-solar
Vision Solar
Chapter 7 — Jul 2021
Vision Solar filed for Chapter 7 liquidation in July 2021, ending the company. It had sold systems in several states.
Systems from 2021 and earlier are now several years old, which is when inverters often start to fail and monitoring connections drift.
If your Vision Solar system is underperforming or showing an inverter error, we can diagnose it and tell you whether the manufacturer will cover the repair.
american-solar-direct
American Solar Direct
Shut down — 2019
American Solar Direct was a California-only installer that shut down in 2019.
Systems installed before 2019 are well into their life. Panels usually keep working, but inverters, monitoring gateways and roof attachments deserve a check.
We can inspect an American Solar Direct system, test production against your bill and tell you what needs attention.
rgs-energy
RGS Energy (Real Goods Solar)
Defunct — 2019
RGS Energy, formerly Real Goods Solar and earlier Alteris Renewables, was delisted and ceased to be an operating residential installer in 2019. It had installed in multiple states.
Permits and paperwork may carry any of its names: RGS Energy, Real Goods Solar or Alteris Renewables.
With the installer long gone, equipment manufacturers are your only warranty source. We handle the diagnosis and the claim paperwork, and do the repair.
verengo
Verengo Solar
Shut down — 2014
Verengo Solar was a California installer that sold mostly in San Diego and Los Angeles counties. It shut down in 2014.
Verengo systems are more than ten years old. Many have had an inverter replaced or have outdated monitoring, and some still have original equipment past its expected life.
We can check an older Verengo system, tell you whether the panels are still producing and what an upgrade or repair would involve.
oneroof-energy
OneRoof Energy
Shut down — 2016
OneRoof Energy was a California-focused solar company that shut down in 2016.
If your OneRoof system was leased or financed, the equipment may be owned by a third party today. Check your documents first.
If the equipment is yours, we can service it. If not, we can still inspect it and document its condition so the owner can act.
kota-energy
Kota Energy
Shut down — about 2022
Kota Energy was an installer focused on Arizona, Texas, Utah and New Mexico that shut down around 2022.
Some Kota customers moved to or own homes in Southern California. The workmanship warranty is gone with the company; the equipment warranties from the manufacturers are not.
If your Kota Energy system is in California, we can diagnose it and file manufacturer claims. Elsewhere, ask us whether we can help.
